summary.title: How to Prepare a Talk
summary.one_liner: Learn a repetition-based method for building a conference talk by speaking it aloud, turning rough note slides into sections, cutting to length, and rehearsing once a day.
keywords: how to prepare a conference talk
building code slides step by step
takeaways: Start by talking out loud about your topic alone, standing and projecting, then note new ideas as brief slides.
Practice once per day, letting partial forgetting keep the talk from becoming robotic, and group the notes into 4 to 8 sections.
Use section intro slides, then cut the least interesting sections and rehearse the transitions until the talk flows.
Aim for a full-length talk of about 25 minutes, and do not add optional parts you might not get to.
Design slides only after the content is settled: keep text large, leave a safety margin, and build tables and code up piece by piece.
summary.summary: The article, by the Deconstruct conference organizer, describes a multi-week talk preparation process built on spoken improvisation rather than writing an outline. The author starts by talking through a topic alone, takes brief note slides, and repeats the talk roughly once a day, so the ideas stabilize while the exact wording keeps changing. Later steps cover grouping notes into sections, trimming content, visual design rules such as font size and safety margins, and advice on timing and day-of-talk habits. It is written as a first-person guide and draws on the author's own experience of about fifty conference talks.
